G-00237.statement: Limited evidence suggests lipedema may be accompanied by lower rates of metabolic comorbidity than in women of similar age in the general population.

G-00238.statement: Routine blood count parameters may not distinguish women with lipedema from controls.

G-00239.statement: Lipedema and lipedema-like peripheral fat distribution may be associated with greater insulin sensitivity than comparable obesity, though findings are mixed.

G-00240.statement: Diabetes is reported less frequently in lipedema and lipedema-like peripheral fat distribution than in comparison groups, although adiposity matching is limited.

G-00241.statement: Lipedema may be associated with a more favorable plasma lipid profile than obesity, though adiposity-matched comparisons are inconsistent.

G-00242.statement: Lipedema is reported to involve systemic and adipose tissue inflammation.

G-00243.statement: A lipedema-like peripheral fat distribution may be inversely associated with cancer prevalence in women.

G-00244.statement: Regionally patterned gluteofemoral fat is proposed to coexist with preserved systemic metabolic health, in contrast to visceral obesity.

G-00248.statement: Circulating testosterone and estradiol are reported not to differ between women with lipedema and controls, though evidence is limited.

merged_twins.statement: Circulating estradiol and testosterone levels in lipedema may not differ from those of controls.

G-00249.statement: Lipedema frequently runs in families, in a pattern suggested to be sex-limited autosomal dominant inheritance with incomplete penetrance.

G-00250.statement: Genome-wide studies suggest common genetic variants may contribute modestly to lipedema susceptibility.

merged_twins.statement: Genome-wide studies report common variant loci associated with a lipedema phenotype, suggesting a modest polygenic contribution.

G-00253.statement: Lipedema is reported almost exclusively in women.

merged_twins.statement: Lipedema affects almost exclusively women.

G-00254.statement: Adipose-derived cells from lipedema may show upregulated adipogenic gene expression compared with controls of similar weight.

G-00257.statement: Liposuction is recommended by many guidelines for selected patients with persistent symptoms despite conservative care, although some restrict it to research settings.

G-00258.statement: Decongestive therapy combined with exercise may reduce limb volume and pain more than pneumatic compression with exercise or exercise alone.

G-00259.statement: Limited evidence suggests conservative measures such as diet and decongestive therapy may improve symptoms in lipedema, with uncertain effect on limb volume.
